minutes.headline: Planning Board released the Butterfly Lane bond and agreed to send the earth removal bylaw forward with the 500 limit.
minutes.summary: With three of five members present, the board released the Butterfly Lane subdivision bond and voted to report the closeout to the selectmen. It reached a consensus for 500 rather than 1,000 in the earth removal article. It also discussed the economic development committee charge (held for a full board), solar bylaw concerns, the Stone Farm bond, and the master plan grant.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board voted to release the bond for the Butterfly Lane subdivision, with three of five members present.
The board voted to send the selectmen a memo reporting that the Butterfly Lane subdivision is closed out and its bond released.
The board reached a consensus to send the earth removal article forward with a limit of 500 rather than 1,000; the town manager is to be told the next morning.
The economic development committee charge was held to the next agenda so all five members can adopt it.
The board heard that the planning assistance grant for the master plan was not received, and will consider whether to request remaining funds at the next Town Meeting.

why_it_matters: The earth removal limit is a bylaw proposal that residents will likely be asked to vote on at Town Meeting, and it sets how much earth removal the town allows.
Without the state planning grant, the master plan may depend on funds that Town Meeting is asked to appropriate, which would draw on the town budget, mostly taxes.
watch_next: The next Planning Board agenda, where the economic development committee charge is to be taken up by all five members.
Whether the board asks the next Town Meeting for remaining master plan funds for one RFP.
